jen_support: FYI customer Acme (INC-9832) is seeing truncated SSE streams followed by immediate reconnects — they report double billing for the same operation. Happened repeatedly over the last hour.

sam_sre: Can you paste the relevant server/proxy logs and the client UA? Also which model/route?

jen_support: Logs attached below. Client uses mobile-sdk-android/1.4.0 behind a corporate proxy. Route: /v1/streams (text generation). Model: model-gpt-8b-quant, batching=auto.

jen_support: ```
marshaler: send chunk id=4 len=1024 -> write: errno=11 (Resource temporarily unavailable)
marshaler: aborting stream connection id=abc123 reason=write-queue-full
nginx: 2026/03/16 14:02:13 [error] 12345#0: *6789 send() not ready (EAGAIN) while sending to client, client: 10.2.3.4, server: _, request: "GET /v1/streams HTTP/1.1"
```

lee_runtime: EAGAIN in user-space marshaller means the client stopped reading and kernel send buffer is full. Are we chunking frequently? How large are token chunks?

jen_support: Default chunking (we pack ~2KB chunks per token batch). Customer reports client processes bytes very slowly (long GC pauses + corp proxy buffering).

maria_prod: This looks like slow-consumer/backpressure. Our runtime currently has a soft write-queue limit; above that we abort to avoid head-of-line blocking other tenants. If the client is slow and the proxy buffers, Nginx backpressure can cascade and cause send() EAGAIN.

sam_sre: Important: the abort path also closes the TCP connection which the mobile SDK interprets as error and immediately reconnects. That reconnect creates another request and billing record. We should confirm if billing dedup keys were present.

jen_support: Customer says they did not set an idempotency key. They saw ~3 reconnections in 30s window and 3 billed sessions.

lee_runtime: Short-term mitigation suggestions: 1) ask customer to upgrade SDK to 1.4.2 (fixes slow-reader buffering), 2) enable smaller chunk size on server (<1KB) and reduce batching window, 3) ask corp proxy team to lower proxy buffering or stream through without full buffering.

maria_prod: Repro steps for ENG: simulate a slow reader using curl/python. Example to reproduce locally - run server then:  ```bash
python - <<'PY'
import socket, time
s = socket.socket()
s.connect(('localhost', 8080))
s.sendall(b"GET /v1/streams HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\n\r\n")
# read one byte, then pause to simulate very slow consumer
print(s.recv(1))
time.sleep(10)
print('done')
PY
```

lee_runtime: Also test with Nginx in front with proxy_buffering on and off. Reprobed on dev and saw same EAGAIN chain within ~6s of slow reads.

sam_sre: Immediate actions: create an incident metric/alert for marshaler EAGAIN aborts and raised abort-rate on streams route. Deploy-bot, can you create an alert in PagerDuty?

deploy-bot: Created PD alert "streams.marshaler.eagain_rate" -> P2. Runbook: reduce chunk size, toggle proxy_buffering, ask customer for SDK upgrade.

jen_support: I'll reach out to customer with a mitigations checklist (SDK patch, disable aggressive proxy buffering, enable smaller chunking) and offer a warm handoff to eng if they want us to test with their proxy config.

lee_runtime: Longer-term: we should change abort behavior to a backoff-retry for transient EAGAINs (try n times with short sleep) instead of immediate full abort. Also add an idempotency header enforcement for streaming billing and server-side billing dedupe for reconnects within short window. Filing RFC-STREAM-41.

maria_prod: Added perf note: consider exposing per-socket write-queue depth and kernel sndbuf usage in our console. That will help customers diagnose slow-consumer issues faster.

sam_sre: Leaving this thread for eng-runtime to take ownership of the fix. Support to update customer.

jen_support: Thanks — updating ticket and pinging customer now. Will post customer confirmation here when done. :white_check_mark:
